case.question: Shortlist three Dubai areas for our takeaway-led pizza and kebab branch.
expected: Three specific candidate areas with evidence
Missing shop rent and footfall acknowledged

answer.headline: Provisional three-area shortlist for a Dubai takeaway-led pizza and kebab branch: Al Barsha/Hessa Street, Deira (Al Muraqqabat–Port Saeed core), and Dubai Marina/JBR — each ranked on competitor overlap and format fit, pending site-level checks.

sections.title: Shortlist and why each area is on it

items.text: Al Barsha / Hessa Street — first candidate. Papa Johns operates a pizza branch at Al Barsha Mall and Allo Beirut runs a Hessa Street branch advertising delivery until 4 AM, so the corridor already shows both a pizza-chain and a late-night Levantine delivery format; that is competitive pressure plus format precedent, not proof of demand or available units. Proximity between these listings does not establish a shared delivery catchment for our site.

Deira (Al Muraqqabat / Port Saeed / City Centre core) — second candidate. Papa Johns lists branches at Al Ghurair Centre in Al Muraqqabat and Deira City Centre in Port Saeed, and the official Dubai neighbourhood guide describes Deira as a heritage district with traditional souks. This suggests a dense, mixed residential/trade district where lean takeaway formats fit conditionally, but the sources do not verify shop rents, footfall, or customer mix. Keep Al Muraqqabat and Port Saeed as separate site searches; proximity does not mean one catchment.

Dubai Marina / JBR — third candidate, only with a differentiation plan. Papa Johns lists a branch at Marina Diamond near Dubai Marina Metro Station; Allo Beirut lists a JBR branch on Al Mamsha Street carrying shawarma, grills and sandwiches; Zaroob lists a Marina restaurant at Radisson Blu Residence advertising 7 AM–5 AM hours. That is three branded operators in overlapping categories, so entry here is contrast-driven (Jordanian-specific meaty pizza and kebab) rather than general pizza/kebab supply.

Competitor presence in these listings is not a demand or market-share measurement, and a branch listing shows a business lists that address, not that we verified it is currently trading. Treat all three areas as candidate search zones until you physically inspect specific units and their surroundings.

sections.title: Pricing signal to build your menu against

items.text: Published Dubai menu references: Allo Beirut's JBR Deliveroo menu lists Pepperoni pizza at AED 40 and Margherita at AED 38; Papa Johns UAE web menu lists All The Meats pizza at AED 33 (8 inch), AED 50 (10 inch) and AED 69 (13 inch). Pizza diameter/weight was not specified for the Allo Beirut items, and these are observed item prices, not checkout totals — delivery charges, extras and tax treatment were not verified. Use them as comparison anchors only, not as a recommended price band.

Proposal: set your own prices after costing your recipes, then price the meaty pizza and kebab sandwich so the two bundles land where customers can compare them against the observed chain and independent anchors above. Test 2–3 price points per item in a limited period before locking a menu; we cannot predict what will sell at which price from these observations.

Delivery channels exist in all three areas: Papa Johns states UAE branches offer delivery and takeaway with a shared menu and prices; Deliveroo describes a UAE partner service using its rider network plus customer pickup, order tracking, and a Marketplace+ option where the restaurant uses its own delivery staff with a selectable delivery area, minimum spend and fees. No commission, fee, radius or service level was verified — get written quotes per area.

If you deliver hot kebab sandwiches and pizza, plan packaging and vehicle checks against Dubai Municipality transport guidance: hot food held at 60 C or above, cold at 5 C or below, frozen at -18 C or below, with sealed containers and hot/cold items separated into insulated secondary units. That guidance is version 2 dated 2023-08-31 and flagged needs_review, so re-check for amendments.

Dubai Municipality guidance requires food handling staff, supervisors and managers to receive formal food safety training appropriate to their activity; also dated 2023-08-31 and flagged needs_review, so confirm the current requirement before hiring. Headcount is a staffing decision you set, not a researched requirement.

sections.title: Research leads: Al Barsha unit supply and kebab competition

items.text: A Dubizzle classified snippet advertises an Italian takeaway pizzeria shop in Al Barsha with annual rent stated at AED 75,000 and a trade licence and Ejari stated valid to May 2026 — the listing is dated January 2026 and is now likely stale or unavailable. This is an uninspected research lead, not a verified rent benchmark; inspect the original page and any current comparable before using any number.

Directory-style snippets suggest kebab and takeout restaurant listings exist in Al Barsha (magicpin, Zomato). These are lead-generation pages, not verified competitor sets; open the original pages to see which operators are actually active.

Core products are meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches positioned on a Jordanian origin.
Target cities are Dubai and Abu Dhabi; this answer covers only the Dubai shortlist you asked for.
Startup budget, monthly rent budget, target audience, positioning and opening date are unset, so no financial test was run.
